rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Algae are photosynthetic, mostly aquatic organisms that lack true roots, stems, and leaves. They are classified into Chrysophyceae (diatoms, golden algae), Pyrrophyceae (dinoflagellates), and Chlorophyceae (green algae). As primary producers, algae generate about half of the world's oxygen and form the base of aquatic food webs. Their economic importance spans food, industry, and agriculture.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Green algae: Chlorophyll a + b, store starch
Brown algae: Chlorophyll a + c + fucoxanthin, store laminarin
Red algae: Chlorophyll a + d + phycobilins, store floridean starch

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Algae are NOT plants in the strict sense: they lack true tissues, roots, and seeds. They are placed in Protista (or Plantae in some systems) depending on the classification used.  ·  Cyanobacteria (blue-green algae) are prokaryotes, not true algae; they are in the domain Bacteria.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB asks for a tabulation of algal groups with pigments, storage products, and examples.  ·  The ecological importance of algae (O₂ production, food web base) is a frequent long-answer topic.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Chlorella pyrenoidosa — green alga, used in bioremediation and food supplements.  ·  Laminaria (kelp) — brown alga, source of alginates and iodine.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Dinoflagellates (Pyrrophyceae) can cause harmful algal blooms (red tides); most algae are harmless.  ·  Chlorophyll content determines the group: green algae have chlorophyll a + b; brown algae (Phaeophyceae) have a + c + fucoxanthin.

rows.text: Algae = A-O-A (Aquatic, Oxygen, Aquatic food base).  ·  Green algae = starch; Brown = laminarin; Red = floridean starch.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Algae are photosynthetic, mostly aquatic, lack true vascular tissues.  ·  Three major groups: Chrysophyceae, Pyrrophyceae, Chlorophyceae.  ·  Ecological role: ~50% of Earth's O₂; base of aquatic food chains.  ·  Reproduction: asexual (spores, fragmentation) + sexual (isogamy, anisogamy, oogamy).

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Algae contribute approximately 50% of global primary oxygen production via photosynthesis.  ·  Diatoms form the base of the oceanic food web; their silica shells accumulate as diatomaceous earth.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: Explain the ecological problem of algal blooms.  ·  What is the storage product in green, brown, and red algae?  ·  Describe the structure and reproduction of a diatom.

rows.label: More hints

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: Porifera-like: Ulva (sea lettuce) — green alga, food in some tropical regions.  ·  Diatom: Navicula — silica-walled, forms diatomaceous earth used in filtration.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Algae: photosynthetic, eukaryotic (mostly), aquatic or damp-environment organisms; no true roots, stems, or leaves.  ·  Major groups: Chrysophyceae (diatoms, golden algae — silica cell walls), Pyrrophyceae (dinoflagellates — bioluminescence, red tides), Chlorophyceae (green algae — Chlorophyll a + b, starch storage).  ·  Reproduction: asexual (spores, fragmentation) and sexual (isogamous, anisogamous, oogamous).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Reproduction (asexual/sexual)  ·  Economic uses  ·  Diatom cell wall: SiO₂ (silica)

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Economic uses: food, industry (agar, alginates), biofertilisers.  ·  Cyanobacteria ≠ true algae (prokaryotic vs eukaryotic).  ·  Algal "stems" and "leaves" are not true vascular tissues; they are structural modifications.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Algal blooms (eutrophication) are an environmental application question.  ·  Differentiate cyanobacteria (prokaryotic) from true algae (eukaryotic).  ·  Memorise pigments and storage products for green, brown, and red algae.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Learn the ecological role of algae (O₂, food web, biogeochemical cycles).  ·  Draw a diatom cell and a green alga (Chlamydomonas or Ulothrix).  ·  List 3 economic uses and 1 environmental problem of algae.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Algae are the primary producers of most aquatic ecosystems.  ·  They contribute approximately 50% of global oxygen via photosynthesis.  ·  Diatoms have silica cell walls and form the base of the marine food web.
